items.summary: US stocks declined on concerns over rising oil prices and higher Treasury yields affecting the market. Investors are cautious due to uncertainty surrounding a potential Iran war peace deal negotiations. Federal Reserve officials hinted at possible interest rate hikes if inflation continues to rise significantly. Nvidia shares surged after announcing a record $150 billion share buyback, while Tesla shares dropped after a lowered price target.

items.summary: Japan's content industry seeks to increase its presence in India through licensing, merchandising, and localization of animation properties. The Doraemon franchise, with over 20 years in India, is now being adapted for theatrical release. The anime market in India is also growing, with streaming platforms expanding their anime offerings significantly. Research shows a high penetration of anime viewership among Indian audiences, indicating potential for commercial growth.

items.title: Agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan asks states to prioritise pulses, oilseeds in rabi crop plans
items.summary: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has asked states to prepare rabi crop plans based on water availability and soil moisture, with water-stressed areas prioritising less water-intensive crops. He also called for higher cultivation of pulses and oilseeds to reduce India’s import dependence, while flagging drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

items.title: Pulses prices surge up to 11% in a month as festive demand, crop concerns bite
items.summary: Prices of key pulses including chana, moong, tur and matar have risen sharply over the past month, with wholesale rates increasing up to 11%, according to IPGA data. Industry executives attributed the surge to growing concerns over crop deficits, moisture stress, lower Australian supplies and stronger festive demand.

items.title: Kerala HC says exorbitant drug prices can trigger government intervention in patented medicines
items.summary: The Kerala High Court ruled that government intervention is permissible for prohibitively priced patented medicines. The court directed the Centre to gather data on the affordability of specific life-saving drugs. This ruling addresses access issues for two breast cancer medications, abemaciclib and ribociclib. The decision empowers the government to consider invoking Section 100 of the Patents Act for affordable access.

items.title: India-UAE trade in rupees, dirhams enters double digits: Piyush Goyal
items.summary: Trade between India and the UAE settled in local currencies has reached double digits, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said Monday. Bilateral trade is also nearing pre-war levels and is expected to recover in coming months. Goyal said businesses are increasingly recognising the benefits of rupee-dirham settlements amid geopolitical disruptions.

items.title: Refiners feel heat physical crude trades higher than futures prices
items.summary: India’s oil refiners are paying significantly more for physical crude than the futures prices making headlines, as constrained Gulf supplies keep the physical market tight. Brent spot prices averaged about $12 a barrel above November futures between September 1 and 22, with the gap widening to as much as $22. Refiners’ actual costs are driven by physical-market benchmarks, grade differentials and contract terms rather than headline futures prices alone.

items.title: Cliffs’ Stelco Set to Idle Some Steel Operations on Tariffs
items.summary: Canadian steelmaker Stelco plans to suspend some operations in Hamilton, Ontario, citing the impact of US tariffs and trade disruptions on the Canadian steel industry.

items.title: Milind Deora backs FSSAI crackdown, says one year is fair for food cos to shift to new labelling
items.summary: Food companies in India are expected to transition to front-of-pack nutrition labeling over the next year. The FSSAI proposed a system including red hexagonal warnings for unhealthy ingredients like sugar and fat. Milind Deora emphasized the importance of immediate nutritional disclosure to inform consumers effectively. Enforcement actions against misleading labels have been supported by Deora as a necessary measure for accountability.

items.title: Gems, jewellery exporters rush to beat new US tariff deadline
items.summary: Mumbai and Surat’s gems and jewellery exporters are stepping up production and rushing shipments to the US ahead of a potential new tariff deadline in October. Units in Mumbai’s SEEPZ and Surat’s diamond-cutting hub have extended working hours to clear Christmas and holiday-season orders before October 16, amid uncertainty over possible duties under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

items.title: Mumbai EOW probes Suraksha Realty promoter’s fraud allegations over Jaiprakash Infratech Deal
items.summary: Mumbai Police’s Economic Offences Wing is probing allegations by Suraksha Realty director Vijaykumar Mohanlal Parekh against fellow promoter Sudhir Walia over alleged cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy in the acquisition of Jaiprakash Infratech. Parekh alleged his group’s consent was bypassed and his brother’s digital signature was used without authorisation.

items.title: FSSAI rules put beverage makers in a tizzy as ‘energy’ deadline looms
items.summary: Red Bull has approached the Delhi High Court to dispute FSSAI's ban on energy drink labeling. The company argues that due process was not followed in the ban's implementation. Reliance has introduced Campa Xtra without the term 'energy' amid the new regulations. Industry executives express concerns about the impact on major energy drink brands in India. The energy drink market is significant, valued at approximately ₹9,500 crore in recent years.

items.title: Jio leads India’s August mobile subscriber additions, Airtel close behind: TRAI
items.summary: Reliance Jio added the most mobile subscribers in India in August at 2.40 million, followed by Bharti Airtel with 2.11 million, Trai data showed. Vodafone Idea added 506,139 users, extending its subscriber growth streak since February. India’s wireless subscriber base rose 5.51 million to 1.293 billion during August.

items.title: Air India's new chief sets sights on higher revenue and cost curbs at first town hall
items.summary: Air India's new CEO Tewolde Gebremariam highlights the importance of financial performance and cost management for the airline. He aims to improve revenue per available seat kilometre and explore opportunities across the network. Employees are encouraged to manage costs at their levels to ensure discipline throughout the organization. Gebremariam also stresses operational reliability and customer confidence through improved punctuality and baggage handling.

The WTO Dispute Settlement Body has agreed to establish a panel to examine Russia’s claims that CBAM creates trade barriers and violates WTO rules.

items.title: Tata Electronics triples equity investment as iPhone, chip plans expand

The company provided ₹61,280 crore in guarantees and ₹1,017 crore in loans to subsidiaries. Equity investments surged to ₹3,727 crore largely due to semiconductor business expansion. Despite a revenue increase, net losses widened significantly to ₹1,611 crore for the fiscal year.

items.title: Gold tumbles 4% to seven-week low as oil, dollar and yields climb
items.summary: Gold fell sharply as rising oil prices heightened inflation concerns and strengthened expectations for tighter monetary policy. A firmer dollar and increasing Treasury yields contributed to the decline in gold prices. Spot gold reached its lowest level since early August, settling significantly lower than previous trading sessions. Other precious metals such as silver, platinum, and palladium also experienced notable declines in their prices.

items.title: IRDAI pushes LIC, SBI Life to seek further cost efficiency
items.summary: Insurers like Life Insurance Corp and SBI Life need to improve cost efficiencies under new regulatory guidelines. The proposals suggest lowering the expense of management limit from around 16% to 12.5% within five years. While larger insurers are compliant, they must reduce their efficiencies further. Smaller players might gain market share if they enhance their operations as well. The overall goal is to increase efficiency and value for policyholders.

items.title: Lakshadweep seaplane launch in limbo after last-minute Skyhop permission withdrawal
items.summary: India's plans for seaplane connectivity in Lakshadweep encountered challenges after permissions were withdrawn unexpectedly. Skyhop, the seaplane operator, had made significant investments in preparation for the launch. Initial approvals were reversed, citing a lack of infrastructure to accommodate seaplanes. This situation highlights ongoing difficulties faced by operators in establishing services on remote routes. The incident reflects broader regulatory and infrastructural issues affecting Indian regional aviation efforts.

items.title: Rains ease peak power demand in September
items.summary: Recent rainfall in India has led to a notable drop in peak power demand, decreasing from 224.7 GW to 218.8 GW before reaching 236.34 GW again. This decline has alleviated some strain on the energy grid. However, an alarming shortage of coal persists, with only eight to nine days' worth of fuel remaining in many plants. Currently, 80 out of 190 coal-based plants are under critical fuel stress.

items.summary: In the first four months of the fiscal year 2026-27, net collections in small savings schemes have surged by an impressive 56% compared to last year, providing a significant boost towards meeting budgetary goals. The appealing savings rates continue to encourage government-backed savings, demonstrating that investor confidence in consistent returns remains strong, even with rising retail participation in the equity markets.

items.title: Trai mandates telcos to take action against spammers identified by their AI-based caller ID
items.summary: Trai has tightened rules against spam calls, mandating telecom operators to act on callers flagged as suspected spammers by AI-based systems even without consumer complaints. Under the new rules, first-time violations can lead to a 15-day outgoing service ban, while repeat offenders may face disconnection of all telecom resources for a year and blacklisting. The rules also introduce changes to spam-call blocking preferences and A2P call charges.

The exemption applies to 20 other jurisdictions that have trade agreements with the US.
